## TL;DR

Healthy running cards keep their concise state labels and expose activity recency through the shared hover and focus tooltip. Silent or stuck cards retain their inline warning signal. Pipeline rows now keep elapsed state time whenever the activity timestamp cannot provide a usable tooltip, including check progress. Touch pinning remains out of scope by owner decision; taps continue to perform their normal action.

## Work and rationale

The final requested fixes were deliberately narrow. PipelineCard already derives a formatted activity tooltip from `lastActivityAt`. Its elapsed visibility rule now needs to treat that tooltip as the deciding condition: when a healthy active row has a valid activity timestamp, recency replaces elapsed time; when the timestamp is absent or invalid, elapsed state time remains visible. The component uses the same visibility condition for the normal status step and the check-progress display, so the fallback remains consistent between the two layouts. Regression coverage exercises both display paths with null and invalid timestamps and confirms elapsed text remains present while no unusable tooltip is exposed.

The declared Board and Pipeline captures use preview fixtures. The Board coding fixture now removes the sample task from paused state and supplies a running start time as well as activity time. The Pipeline fixture's agent seeding helper also clears paused state before marking each relevant task running. The shot declarations target the corresponding coding status element and hover it to show the popover, so the capture represents the requested running state and interaction.

The shared tooltip's touch gesture logic was left as previously removed. This follows the owner's updated scope: touch support belongs with the upcoming mobile rewrite, while this task verifies mouse hover and keyboard focus.

## Approaches tried

I checked the latest review report and the component's shared status and tooltip path before changing the narrow fallback coverage. Rather than introducing separate timing behavior for status and check progress, the tests exercise both render paths against the same component rule. I also corrected the fixture seed itself instead of changing screenshot expectations, because the paused output came from stale pause state carried into a fixture that was intended to depict coding.

The branch was behind main, and the requested main merge had already begun when this turn resumed. Main's copy of the task file includes the owner-approved scope section, so that is the copy selected for conflict resolution. Main also changed other tracked files as part of its upstream progress; those changes were not authored as part of this task.

## Challenges and blockers

The prior handoff failed because the two captures displayed paused cards, and review reported that Pipeline elapsed time disappeared without a usable activity timestamp. The paused state is inherited from shared preview-store state unless each fixture explicitly clears it. The elapsed fallback depends on the validity of the formatted tooltip, not merely whether the raw timestamp field is non-null.

The merge with main is currently in progress with the task-file conflict resolved in the working tree. This environment's task instructions prohibit running `git add` or `git commit`, while completing a Git merge requires staging the resolved conflict and creating a merge commit. I have not staged or committed. The required scoped RepoOS check and handoff remain dependent on resolving that workflow constraint.

## Key learnings

Preview fixtures should establish all mutually exclusive state explicitly. Adding a task to `runningIds` is insufficient if `pausedIds` can retain the same ID from fixture setup. Similarly, conditional replacement UI should hide its fallback only when the replacement content is actually available and valid. This applies equally when multiple render branches present the same underlying timing information.
